text:
jeremy_sales: Heads-up — Auric (large fintech) wants a short POC. Key asks: validate our hosted runtime with their 4-bit quantized 30B fork, confirm KV-cache compatibility for long conversations (seq 4096), KMS + EU data residency answers, and a POC cost estimate. Can ENG/ML/Sec ops weigh in?

anya_engineer: Need artifact format (HF/adapter/merged), tokenizer type, and whether they used per-channel quantization or PTQ. Also, seq=4096 is big — will need model slicing / prefaulting checks.

li_research: They said HF bundle, merged weights preferred but they may send adapters (LoRA). Model uses 30B arch, vocab ~50k. For 4-bit please confirm block-size (32/128) — that affects kernel choices.

zoe_security: Security questions: will POC be hosted in eu-west-1 only? They require KMS with customer-managed keys and an answer on prompt retention. Also ask if we can sign their standard security questionnaire (they attached a spreadsheet).

pat_ops: Ops checklist for hosted POC: 1) model validation 2) ephemeral catalog entry 3) traffic shaping/rate caps 4) monitoring + logs. Sample registration command:
```bash
rwdctl model add 
  --id auric-poc-30b 
  --artifact s3://auric/poc/auric-30b-hf.tar.gz 
  --quant 4bit 
  --region eu-west-1
```
We'll enforce a 100 RPS cap by default and enable sampling for traces.

pricing-bot: Pricing estimator: hosted POC: estimated token cost $0.012/token (~decode-only) assuming batchable workload; Dedicated estimate TBD after traffic commit.

anya_engineer: Perf rough numbers (internal A6000-like): single replica, batch=1, seq=512 decode p95 ~180ms per token; at seq=4096 we expect memory pressure and p95 could be 2.5x. Dynamic batching can recover throughput but may increase latency variance.

li_research: Also flag: KV-cache layout for seq>2048 requires checking kv index dims. Ask them to run our kv-diagnostic (small script) — we can send it.

jeremy_sales: They want to know if runtime supports on-the-fly LoRA stacking for experiments.

anya_engineer: Short answer: runtime can apply adapters at load time, but stacking at serve-time (hot-swap) is experimental and adds ~5-10% latency and memory overhead. Recommend merged weights for POC to reduce risk.

zoe_security: For the questionnaire: we can confirm KMS integration (customer key supported), TLS, audit logs retention configurable, and EU-only region deployment. On prompts: default is ephemeral by product policy; we can enable retention for troubleshooting with opt-in and SOC docs. I'll draft answers.

pat_ops: Small runbook snippet for onboarding: 1) validate artifact (rwd-validate) 2) build container (rwd-build) 3) register ephemeral model 4) smoke load test 5) flip monitoring to 1s granularity. Example validate command:
```bash
# validate HF artifact
rwd-validate --artifact s3://auric/poc/auric-30b-hf.tar.gz --expect-arch 30B --out /tmp/auric-validate.json
```
If checksum + layers OK -> build.

li_research: Requesting also their sample prompt set (10-20 conversational threads) to run quality/perf mix tests. Helps estimate token mix and batchability.

jeremy_sales: I'll ask Auric for merged weights, the sample prompt set, and the signed security spreadsheet. They want a POC quote today to budget.

pricing-bot: If POC stays <2k peak tokens/s and no custom SLAs, we can offer a fixed POC bundle: $5k flat + $0.009/token for decode above bundled 500k tokens. If they convert to Dedicated within 60 days, waive setup fee.

anya_engineer: For timelines: given artifacts + prompt set by EOD, ENG can validate and smoke test in 48 hours, perf doc ready in 72 hours. If they require on-the-fly adapters add +3 days.

zoe_security: ETA for security spreadsheet answers: EOD tomorrow. Will include DPA excerpt and KMS flow diagram.

pat_ops: Also note: we need license grant allowing us to run in eval env. Ask legal sign-off from their side.

jeremy_sales: Great. Action items: 1) I’ll request merged artifact, prompt set, and security spreadsheet from Auric (today) 2) ENG will run validation and perf smoke once we have artifact (48-72h) 3) Security to return spreadsheet answers EOD tomorrow 4) Pricing team to confirm POC bundle and Dedicated uplift.

jeremy_sales: Anyone object to that plan?

anya_engineer: No objections.

li_research: Fine by me.

zoe_security: Sounds good.

pricing-bot: Pricing note posted to thread: POC bundle draft submitted.

jeremy_sales: Thanks all — I'll reply back to Auric and post their artifact link here when available. :thumbsup:
